stories.headline: Nvidia drops $3.5 billion on MediaTek to pull more chip partners into its orbit
stories.blurb: Nvidia is investing $3.5 billion in Taiwan's MediaTek, aiming to expand the number of chipmakers designing hardware that works with its data center infrastructure. The deal deepens ties with a company that already makes processors for phones, cars, and smart home devices—potentially bringing Nvidia's AI reach beyond the server rack.
stories.why_it_matters: Nvidia is locking in partners to keep competitors from building rival AI chip ecosystems
stories.original_headline: Nvidia Makes $3.5 Billion Bet on MediaTek

stories.headline: ChatGPT now falls under EU's strictest tech regulations
stories.blurb: The EU just classified ChatGPT as a Very Large Online Search Engine under the Digital Services Act, meaning OpenAI must now actively mitigate risks around minors, user mental health, and illegal content. The rules apply the same accountability framework used for Google and Bing to AI chat.
stories.why_it_matters: First major AI chatbot to get the same regulatory treatment as traditional search engines.
stories.original_headline: ChatGPT to face tougher regulation in the EU

stories.headline: This AI startup searches video like Google searches text—and just hit $250M valuation
stories.blurb: Clipto, a three-year-old company, lets you search inside massive video libraries by asking questions in plain English. It hit $15 million in revenue and profitability before raising its latest $15 million round at a $250 million valuation.
stories.why_it_matters: Video search has been unsolved for years—if this works at scale, every industry sitting on footage gold mines can finally use it.
stories.original_headline: Clipto uses AI to search terabytes of video and is now valued at $250M

stories.headline: Sony and Warner are suing Anthropic for copyright infringement
stories.blurb: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell filed suit in California federal court claiming Claude reproduced tens of thousands of copyrighted song lyrics without permission. They're seeking up to $150,000 per work plus $25,000 each time copyright information was removed.
stories.why_it_matters: First major music publisher lawsuit against a frontier AI lab over training data
stories.original_headline: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
